questions.stem: According to the passage, what was China's for-profit tutoring industry valued at before the 2021 crackdown?
options: About $10 billion
About $50 billion
About $100 billion
About $200 billion
questions.evidence: Before the policy change, China's for-profit tutoring industry was valued at about $100 billion.
questions.explanation_ko: 정책 변경 이전 중국의 영리 과외 산업 가치는 약 1,000억 달러였다고 나와 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following was NOT a stated goal of the original 2021 "double reduction" policy?
options: Reducing financial pressure on families
Creating equal educational chances for rich and poor families
Eliminating poor quality tutoring services
Increasing tuition fees at public schools
questions.evidence: The reported aim was to reduce financial pressure on families. It was also meant to create equal educational chances for both rich and poor families and to eliminate poor quality tutoring services.
questions.explanation_ko: 가정의 재정적 부담 완화, 빈부 간 교육 기회 균등, 저품질 과외 근절이 목표로 언급되지만 공립학교 학비 인상은 언급되지 않았습니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from Yang Zengdong's worry that only wealthy families can afford private tutors?
options: The crackdown successfully closed the academic gap between rich and poor families.
The crackdown may have unintentionally widened the gap between rich and poor students, the opposite of its original goal.
Private tutoring has completely disappeared in China.
Only poor families can now afford private tutors.
questions.evidence: the academic gap between rich people and everyone else will get worse
questions.explanation_ko: 부유한 가정만 개인 과외를 감당할 수 있어 빈부 격차가 커질 것이라는 우려에서, 단속이 애초 목표였던 교육 형평성 달성에 실패했을 수 있음을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that tutoring centers often renamed math classes as "logical thinking" classes?
options: To illustrate how tutoring businesses found ways around the 2021 restrictions
To explain a new teaching method for mathematics
To criticize logical thinking as a subject
To show that math classes became more popular after the ban
questions.evidence: To get around the rules, tutoring centers would often rename classes.
questions.explanation_ko: 이 예시는 과외 업체들이 2021년 규제를 피해 갈 방법을 찾았음을 보여 주기 위한 것입니다.

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "crackdown" mean?
options: a celebration event
a strong government effort to stop or control something
a type of scholarship
a new school subject
questions.evidence: The crackdown cost the industry billions of dollars.

그는 그 정책이 가정에 어려운 선택을 안겨 주었다고 말했다.

key_points: China is quietly easing its 2021 'double reduction' crackdown on for-profit tutoring, which had aimed to reduce financial pressure on families and create more equal educational opportunities.
The crackdown had cost the roughly $100 billion tutoring industry billions of dollars and tens of thousands of jobs, but demand from parents for tutoring never disappeared.

Government moves to ease restrictions have sped up recently, including a State Council plan to boost spending that includes education services, partly to help millions of new university graduates find jobs.

Some worry that expensive one-on-one tutoring, which thrived even during the crackdown, has widened the academic gap between wealthy and less wealthy families, the opposite of the policy's original goal.
main_idea: China is quietly loosening its 2021 crackdown on private tutoring companies to help support economic growth and jobs, even though the crackdown may have widened, rather than closed, the educational gap between rich and poor families.
restate_sentence: China is quietly easing regulations on private education companies as the government aims to support a slowing economy.
